newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends easy, gilts up in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends easy, gilts up in active trade.

text.p: Indian call money ended Monday at 6.25-6.50 percent down from opening quotes of 7.25-7.75 percent, dealers said.
They said most of Monday's deals were in the 6.75-7.25 percent range.

"Call money rates will be around 6.0 percent for the rest of the week," a dealer at a state-run bank said. "They will not fall further as inflows through interest payments will largely be absorbed by food credit disbursals."
Dealers said more than 20 billion rupees will flow into the banking system before the end of May through interest payments on government securities.
Easier call money triggered buying interest in securities, pushing prices up in brisk trade, dealers said.
They said prices rose by 10-15 paise on stocks with short- and medium-term maturities.

The 13.40 percent government stock 1999 rose to 104.55 rupees from its last traded 104.35 rupees, the 13.50 percent 1998 stock improved to 103.10 rupees from 102.92 rupees while the 12.69 percent 2007 stock rose to 100.35 rupees from 100.23, dealers said.

The yield on October-maturity 364-day treasury bills fell to 8.50 percent from 8.65 percent, March maturity to 9.28 percent from 9.40 and February maturity to 9.28 percent yield from 9.3 percent, dealers said.
January maturity treasury bill was in demand on Monday with trades worth 400 million rupees at a yield of 9.25 percent, dealers said.
One secondary market trade at a yield of 7.85 percent was reported in commercial paper maturing on May 28, dealers said.
